facts.statement: Rhinorex is a genus of kritosaurin hadrosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Neslen Formation in central Utah.
facts.quote: Rhinorex is a genus of kritosaurin hadrosaur from the Late Cretaceous Neslen Formation, in central Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen BYU 13258 consists of a mostly articulated partial skeleton including the skull, vertebral column, partial pelvis, and skin impressions.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen BYU 13258 is composed of a partial but mostly articulated skeleton, which includes the skull, the vertebral column, a partial pelvis, and skin impressions.

facts.statement: The genus name Rhinorex means "nose king", derived from the Greek word rhinos and the Latin word rex.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Greek word "rhinos" which means "nose", and the Latin word "rex" which means "king."

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Rhinorex is Rhinorex condrupus.
facts.quote: The type and only species known is Rhinorex condrupus.

facts.statement: Rhinorex belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae.
Rhinorex is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Rhinorex is a member of the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
Rhinorex lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Rhinorex is a close relative of Gryposaurus, with some researchers proposing it should be classified within that genus.
facts.quote: It is likely a close relative of Gryposaurus, and indeed some have suggested that it falls within the genus Gryposaurus, as the phylogenetic analysis indicates.

facts.statement: The presence of Rhinorex challenges the hypothesis of provincialism in Late Cretaceous Laramidian dinosaur faunas.
facts.quote: This would challenge the idea of provincialism in Late Cretaceous Laramidian faunas.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Rhinorex inhabited more coastal environments than its relative Gryposaurus.
facts.quote: It may be that Rhinorex lived in more coastal environments than Gryposaurus.

rejected.statement: Although its exact age is uncertain, Rhinorex probably lived 75 million years ago and was discovered in estuarine sediments.
rejected.quote: Its exact placement in time is uncertain, though it probably dates to 75 million years ago and was discovered in estuarine sediments.
